excerpt: In the Kelly et al. task, rapid letter streams were presented to both hemifields at rates from 9.45 to 17.01 Hz, with each stimulus lasting 11 ms. After a central arrow cue, alpha power ipsilateral to the cued direction increased above pre-cue baseline, no contralateral decreases were observed, and bilateral stimulation continued throughout the trial.
overview: This is the review's key answer to the idling objection. By maintaining bilateral visual stimulation, the design reduces the chance that alpha asymmetry simply reflects recovery from cue-induced desynchronization. The observed above-baseline alpha increase therefore supports active suppression of the ignored stream.
title: Bilateral Stream Baseline Test
